metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to code (usually PRs), QEPs/design proposals, issues/security vulnerabilities, and comments/feedback on PRs.

evidence.quote: there must be a human in the loop. Contributors must read and review all Large Language Model (LLM)-generated code or text before they ask other project members to review it.
The contributor is always the author and is fully accountable for their contributions.

Code, usually in the form of a pull request
- QEPs or design proposals
- Issues or security vulnerabilities
- Comments and feedback on pull requests

domains.reasoning: The policy names code, PRs, issues and comments explicitly, sets a human-in-the-loop supervision level, requires disclosure/labelling, and states the contributor is always accountable as author.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The document is scoped to contributions (code, QEPs, issues, comments) and review tooling; it never discusses recording or transcribing meetings or small-group discussions.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Covers QEPs/design proposals and gives documentation as a worked example of approved use.

evidence.quote: using an LLM to generate documentation, which a contributor manually reviews for correctness, edits, and then posts as a PR, is an approved use of tools under this policy.

domains.reasoning: Documentation and design proposals are explicitly named as content types covered, with the same human-in-the-loop supervision and contributor accountability applied generally across the policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use for moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The document describes human maintainers applying the 'extractive' label, locking conversations, closing PRs, or banning contributors, but never discusses whether AI may be used to perform or assist moderation actions.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Automated review tools that publish comments without human oversight; opt-in tools keeping a human in the loop are acceptable.

evidence.quote: automated review tools that publish comments without human review are not allowed. However, an opt-in review tool that keeps a human in the loop is acceptable under this policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for AI-assisted review output
domains.reasoning: The policy directly names automated/AI review tools and sets a human-in-the-loop supervision level (banning fully autonomous public comments), but never states who is accountable for the content of AI-assisted reviews.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Agents that take action in digital project spaces without human approval, e.g. the GitHub @claude agent.

evidence.quote: An important implication of this policy is that it bans agents that take action in our digital spaces without human approval, such as the GitHub @claude agent.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for autonomous agent actions
domains.reasoning: Autonomous/agentic use is named explicitly and banned, but the policy does not state who would be accountable if such an agent were used or approved a human action on its behalf.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule or mention of energy/water/carbon impact
domains.reasoning: The document's cost concerns are entirely about maintainer time and attention ('extractive contributions'), not energy, water, or carbon footprint; environmental impact is not raised even as rationale.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule or mention of server load or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: The policy's scarcity concern is maintainer review time/energy, not server load, CI strain, or hardware financing; infrastructure strain is not discussed.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Artificial intelligence systems raise many questions around copyright that have yet to be answered. ... Using AI tools to regenerate copyrighted material does not remove the copyright
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on data used to train AI tools themselves
domains.reasoning: The Copyright section addresses copyrighted material appearing in AI-assisted contributions (an output-side concern) and voices unresolved concern about AI and copyright, but sets no rule about what data may be used to train AI systems or platform user data usage.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The policy is a specific, human-in-the-loop framework for contributions, documentation/QEPs, and review tooling (banning fully autonomous agents and unreviewed automated review comments) with contributor accountability, but it never addresses notetaker bots, moderation, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, or training-data use, and leaves accountability unnamed for review and autonomous-agent scenarios.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
